subject: general
question: Which of the following disputes falls under the Supreme Court's exclusive original jurisdiction as per Article 131 of the Indian Constitution?

options.text: Election disputes of MPs and MLAs
Disputes between Centre and one or more States

solution:
The correct answer is __**Disputes between Centre and one or more States**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Article 131 of the Indian Constitution provides the **exclusive original jurisdiction** of the Supreme Court of India in certain disputes.
 
• These disputes include those between the Government of India and one or more States or between two or more States.
 
• The Supreme Court's original jurisdiction is called "exclusive" because it cannot be exercised by any other court in India.
 
• The jurisdiction applies only to legal matters and not political disputes or policy matters.
 
• This provision ensures the role of the Supreme Court as the **final arbiter** in resolving disputes concerning the interpretation of the Constitution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Key Jurisdictions of the Supreme Court of India:
 
 
• **Original Jurisdiction (Article 131):**

 
 
• Hears disputes between the Government of India and States, or between States themselves, involving questions of law or fact.
 
• Writ Jurisdiction (Article 32): Enforces Fundamental Rights by issuing writs like Habeas Corpus, Mandamus, Prohibition, Quo Warranto, and Certiorari.
 
 
 
• **Appellate Jurisdiction:**
 
 
• The final court of appeal, hearing appeals from High Courts in constitutional, civil, criminal, and special leave petition (SLP) cases.
 
 
 
• **Advisory Jurisdiction (Article 143):**
 
 
• Advises the President on matters of public importance or law, though these are not binding.
 
 
 
• **Review Jurisdiction:**
 
 
• Power to review its own judgments or orders.
 
 
 
• **Extraordinary & Other Powers:**
 
 
• Transfer of Cases: Can transfer civil/criminal cases between High Courts or subordinate courts.
 
• Suo Moto Powers: Can take up cases on its own motion.
 
• Article 142: Powers to pass orders for "complete justice".
